claims.statement: A live-mode Stripe restricted API key (RAK) starts with rk_live_.

sources.supports: Live mode keys start with pk_live_, rk_live_ and sk_live_; the key-types table gives rk_ as the Restricted API key (RAK) prefix.
A restricted API key (RAK) starts with rk_live_ or rk_test_.

claims.statement: A sandbox restricted key starts with rk_test_; the mode segment (live_ or test_) separates rk_live_ from rk_test_ and the first segment (pk_, rk_, sk_) names the key type.

sources.supports: Sandbox keys start with pk_test_ for publishable keys, rk_test_ for restricted keys and sk_test_ for secret keys.

claims.statement: A restricted key is not safe to expose: only publishable keys (pk_) are documented as safe to expose outside the backend, and restricted keys are named among the keys the account holder must protect.

sources.supports: Only publishable keys are safe to expose outside your application's backend; you are responsible for protecting other Stripe API keys, including restricted API keys.
Treat RAKs with the same caution as secret API keys; a RAK is an API key your server-side applications include in Stripe API requests.

claims.statement: Two pinned scanner rules by different maintainers are both consistent with rk_live_ followed by a run of 20 to 99 ASCII letters or digits: gitleaks 8.30.1 stripe-access-token matches (?:sk|rk)_(?:test|live|prod)_ plus [a-zA-Z0-9]{10,99}, and trufflehog 3.97.4 stripe detector matches [rs]k_live_ plus [a-zA-Z0-9]{20,247}. The overlap is a lexical range, not a documented grammar, and says nothing about issued keys.

sources.supports: gitleaks v8.30.1 config/gitleaks.toml rule stripe-access-token: [a-zA-Z0-9]{10,99} after the sk|rk _ test|live|prod _ prefix.

claims.statement: Whether the body of a restricted key is exactly 32 characters is not established: the Stripe pages state no body length or alphabet, and neither pinned scanner rule fixes the length at 32 (they accept ranges). The earlier revision's wording that a 32-character body is tool-corroborated is not supported by those rules; 32 lies inside the overlap above but is not singled out by it.

sources.supports: The keys page names the rk_live_ and rk_test_ prefixes and gives no body length or alphabet.
gitleaks v8.30.1 accepts a 10 to 99 character body.
trufflehog v3.97.4 accepts a 20 to 247 character body.

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed. Revision 2 isolates the restricted-key claims that revision 1 inherited from the shared legacy 'stripe-token' contract (organization-key statements are not restated here; see stripe:organization-api-key) and corrects the revision-1 wording that a 32-character body is tool-corroborated, which the pinned scanner rule ranges do not show. Key rotation and expiry (#112) are out of scope.
